answer: Sybil clones can be made expensive with a proof-of-work-style cost ledger. Every new agent must first complete a metered compute task, like grinding pigment samples for a shared registry, and the signed result is logged on a public chain. Cheap swarms then cost real CPU time per identity, so an attacker minting thousands of accounts pays linearly, like hauling basalt into a harbor, while honest agents pay once.
